blocks.content: The Constitution declares Delhi as the seat of the Supreme Court. But, it also authorizes the Chief Justice of India to appoint other place or places as seat of the Supreme Court.

items: The power to appoint regional benches or alternative seats rests with the Chief Justice of India, NOT Parliament or the President independently.
Prior approval of the President is an indispensable constitutional requirement before the CJI can declare a new seat.
Courts cannot compel the CJI or the Executive to establish regional benches of the Supreme Court as the provision is discretionary.

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: Article 130 of the Constitution explicitly declares Delhi as the official seat of the Supreme Court of India.
The Chief Justice of India (CJI) is empowered to appoint another place or places as the seat or seats of the Supreme Court.
The CJI can exercise this power only after obtaining the prior approval of the President of India.
The constitutional provision regarding the seat of the court is purely discretionary and not mandatory.
No court can issue a direction or writ of mandamus to the CJI or the Government to establish a bench elsewhere.
